run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The one entity demonstrably broken is the frontend-proxy Deployment in namespace astronomy-shop. At 12:00:33 a config-only rollout created ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 (revision 2) with the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy and the same 65Mi memory limit as revision 1 (frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5), but with an additional duplicate env entry FRONTEND_HOST=localhost in the pod template; the old pod was stopped at 12:00:34. The new pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-vfrb7 became not-ready, was OOMKilled (exit code 137, last OOM at 12:01:35), reached restartCount 3 and is in CrashLoopBackOff; the Deployment reports unavailableReplicas 1 and Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable). The frontend-proxy Service now has no ready endpoint addresses (only notReadyAddresses for that pod), while all other 22 services in the namespace have ready endpoints. Requests from the load-generator that reached the shop after the proxy was replaced failed: three GET spans of 8.8-9.6s ending in requests.exceptions.ConnectionError ('Remote end closed connection without response') and a POST ending in ConnectionResetError(104, 'Connection reset by peer'), all started 12:00:40-12:00:41. Immediately before the replacement, the same POST /api/checkout path through frontend-proxy returned 200. The exact mechanism by which the extra FRONTEND_HOST=localhost entry makes envoy fail (hypothesised: the frontend upstream is pointed at the proxy's own listener on localhost:8080, giving hanging self-looped requests and memory growth into the 65Mi limit) is a hypothesis: the container logs inside the authorized window are not retrievable and no memory series exists for the new pod. All flagd fault-injection flags in flagd-config were off, and locust_errors did record HTTP 500s on /api/checkout (5) and /api/data (4) by 12:00:46 whose timing and cause could not be resolved.

claims.text: At 12:00:49 all 27 astronomy-shop pods were Running with all containers ready and restartCount 0, including the then-current frontend-proxy pod; this is the pre-failure baseline for the namespace.

Pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-vfrb7 (created 2026-11-21T12:00:33Z) has its frontend-proxy container not ready: lastState terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 finishedAt 2026-11-21T12:01:35Z, restartCount 3, current state waiting/CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 20s restarting failed container'), and pod conditions Ready=False and ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady.

Deployment frontend-proxy reports observedGeneration 2, replicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 and condition Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ('Deployment does not have minimum availability') at 12:01:36Z, while all other 22 deployments in the namespace report readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1.

The frontend-proxy Deployment was rolled with an unchanged pod template image and unchanged resource limits: ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 (revision 1, created 11:59:35Z, scaled to 0) and ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 (revision 2, created 12:00:33Z, 1 replica) both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy with resources limits.memory 65Mi and identical command/annotations.

The only template difference between revision 1 and revision 2 is an extra duplicate env entry: revision 2 carries FRONTEND_HOST=frontend early in the list and an additional FRONTEND_HOST with value localhost after OTEL_COLLECTOR_PORT_HTTP, which revision 1 does not have; the live Deployment spec contains both entries (FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FRONTEND_HOST=frontend ... FRONTEND_HOST=localhost).

Deployment frontend-proxy events show 'Scaled up replica set frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 from 0 to 1' and 'Scaled down replica set frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 from 1 to 0' at 12:00:33-12:00:34Z, and Pod event 'Stopping container frontend-proxy' on frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-xqptm at 12:00:34Z; no event names any other actor applying a change to this workload.

Service endpoints at 12:04:05: frontend-proxy has ready addresses [] and notReadyAddresses [frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-vfrb7]; every other service in astronomy-shop (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, grafana, image-provider, kafka, llm, opensearch, otel-collector, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) has ready addresses and no notReady addresses.

load-generator error spans started 12:00:40.455Z, 12:00:40.722Z and 12:00:41.192Z: three GET spans lasting 8.81-9.56s whose error detail is requests.exceptions.ConnectionError ('Connection aborted.', RemoteDisconnected('Remote end closed connection without response')) and one POST span spanning 19ms with ConnectionResetError(104, 'Connection reset by peer'), i.e. requests issued right after the frontend-proxy pod replacement failed to get a response.

Before the replacement, traffic still succeeded: trace efe4347cd45a8eeb95799e802be3bffa (start 12:00:25Z) shows load-generator POST -> frontend-proxy 'POST' and 'router frontend egress' spans with http.status_code 200, frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 200, checkout PlaceOrder rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and email POST /send_order_confirmation 200.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) has every fault-injection flag ENABLED but with defaultVariant 'off': llmInaccurateResponse, llmRateLimitError, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak.

locust_errors at 12:00:46Z recorded HTTP 500 responses with messages "HTTPError('500 Server Error: Internal Server Error for url: /api/checkout')" (value 5), "/api/data/" (1), "/api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars" (2) and "/api/data/?contextKeys=telescopes" (1); the counters are cumulative and their timing cannot be resolved from this sample.

In the sampled frontend traces (backend data 12:00:25-12:00:34Z, 469 spans) no span of frontend, cart, checkout, product-catalog, currency, email, shipping, quote, recommendation, ad or flagd carries an error status, and the frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-9k25s was Ready with 0 restarts.

The Deployment's added FRONTEND_HOST=localhost entry makes envoy resolve its 'frontend' upstream to its own listener on localhost:8080, so client requests are re-routed into the proxy itself, hang without a response (the observed 8.8-9.6s ConnectionError requests) and accumulate buffers until the container hits the 65Mi limit and is OOMKilled; this would explain why the identical image and identical memory limit were healthy in revision 1 and fatal in revision 2.

The locust HTTP 500 counts on POST /api/checkout and GET /api/data may be a startup transient of the namespace-wide rollout at 11:59:35Z (all 26 other pods were created within 11:59:35-11:59:38Z) rather than a second independent fault, since the retained traces show only 200/0 statuses from frontend and its dependencies and no 500 span was found.

The frontend-proxy crash is not explained by an image or resource-limit change: both ReplicaSets use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy and limits.memory 65Mi, and the revision-1 pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-xqptm ran with restartCount 0 at the same limit.

A flagd feature-flag fault (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, kafkaQueueProblems, adHighCpu, adManualGc, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse) being switched on is not supported: the flagd-config ConfigMap declares defaultVariant 'off' for every one of these flags, and no span in the sampled traces shows a flagd or downstream error.

gaps: No application log line from pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-vfrb7 lies inside the authorized window (all 121 readable lines were after 12:00:46Z and the previous instance had no lines), so the exact crash message and whether envoy logged a self-referencing upstream or memory pressure could not be verified.

No container memory or limit metric series exists for pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-vfrb7 at the window end (only the deleted pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-xqptm was present), so the hypothesized memory ramp to the 65Mi limit is unverified.

Prometheus returned a single sample per series at/about 12:00:46Z (e.g. locust and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready), so error-rate and latency trends, and any baseline for comparison, could not be computed; the locust HTTP 500 counts cannot be attributed to a time or to a specific downstream service.

Who or what changed the frontend-proxy Deployment pod template at 12:00:33Z (Helm release astronomy-shop, chart opentelemetry-demo-0.40.4) is unknown because no change-history integration is available; Helm release data is stored in secrets, which cannot be read.
The flagd runtime flag state (as opposed to the flagd-config ConfigMap defaults) could not be read, so a runtime flag toggle cannot be fully excluded.

The load-generator pod itself is absent from the cluster inventory (deployment load-generator reports 1 ready replica and its metrics are scraped from load-generator.astronomy-shop:9646), so its logs could not be read.
Impact on real customers or on the frontend service's own request success rate was not observed; only load-generator client spans show failed requests.
next_steps: Read the current and previous container logs of pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-vfrb7 outside the authorized window to capture the envoy startup and crash output.
Diff the frontend-proxy Deployment against the opentelemetry-demo-0.40.4 chart defaults for Helm release astronomy-shop to identify where the second FRONTEND_HOST=localhost entry was introduced.

If the duplicate env entry is confirmed to be the cause, remove it from the frontend-proxy Deployment pod template (keeping FRONTEND_HOST=frontend) and roll out, then confirm the pod stays Ready beyond a few minutes.
Check the flagd runtime flag values (flagd UI/API) rather than only the flagd-config ConfigMap to exclude a runtime fault-flag toggle.
Query container_memory_working_set_bytes for the new frontend-proxy pod over a later window to confirm whether memory rises to the 65Mi limit before each OOMKill.
